summary:
New A1 direction this turn: the path from committed decision to applied state, and how the FSM-side index is used for snapshot metadata.

Explained (source-only, no defect): the FSM thread's applied index legitimately lags committed configuration entries, but the lag is contained by an explicit guard rather than a silent mislabel. Committed entries reach the FSM thread only when prepareLog builds a tuple (raft.go:1362-1387): LogBarrier and LogCommand always, LogConfiguration only when protocolVersion > 2, while LogNoop and the deprecated peer entries return nil and are never dispatched — processLogs (raft.go:1292-1358) responds to their futures itself and then advances lastApplied. In the FSM thread (fsm.go:92-125) every received entry advances the local lastIndex/lastTerm except a LogConfiguration when the FSM has no ConfigurationStore, which returns early with that stated reason; the snapshot request reports that index (fsm.go:216-233). takeSnapshot (snapshot.go:125-211) then reads the committed configuration from the main thread and refuses when snapReq.index < committedIndex, so metadata is never labelled with a configuration the FSM has not reached, and compaction stays bounded by min(snapshot index, last log index - TrailingLogs) (snapshot.go:213-240). The observable boundary is that snapshot creation keeps failing with 'cannot take snapshot now, wait until the configuration entry at N has been applied' until an entry the FSM accounts for arrives — and both a command and a Barrier traverse that path, so the condition is self-clearing under the library's own client contract. No liveness defect is claimed.

Paused, sourced open question with its own necessary gap (no claim, no execution requested): shouldSnapshot (snapshot.go:104-120) subtracts the snapshot index from the log store's LastIndex with unsigned arithmetic and no ordering guard, while the snapshot-aware index used elsewhere is max(lastLogIndex, lastSnapshotIndex) (state.go:159-163). A node that recovers through InstallSnapshot sets its snapshot index to the snapshot index (raft.go:1930-1950) while its log store may keep a lower index, since compaction is bounded by the log head; if a run reaches that state, the automatic condition would be permanently true and the node would create a fresh full-state snapshot every SnapshotInterval until its log store grows past that index. Registered with a discriminator (drive a real InstallSnapshot recovery and sample log-store index, snapshot index, shouldSnapshot and repeated snapshot creation), resume conditions, and an explicit note that only the condition is in question and the visible effect would be repeated snapshot work, not a stated safety or availability failure.

Knowledge promoted: prepareLog routing rules, FSM-thread index advancement (including the early return), takeSnapshot's representability guard and compact bound, getLastIndex = max(lastLogIndex, lastSnapshotIndex), and the unsigned delta in shouldSnapshot. Validation of these bytes returns valid:true; earlier drafts and receipts are untouched.
